goal: Free chart is the hook. Account required. Reports, extra charts and a subscription are what sells.

event.label: Kaycee's event
event.target: Phase 1 live: self-serve free chart with account signup

phases.title: Phase 1 — Free chart, self-serve
phases.why: A stranger on the website gets a real chart in ten seconds, in the cloud, and leaves an email behind.

items.title: Chart builder reads the library from Supabase, not the local cache
items.note: Done 9 September. Proved by building a chart with the local library moved away entirely. Notion multi-selects and relations are normalised so the database and the file produce byte-identical charts.

items.title: Charts become database rows, not a hardcoded roster
items.note: Applied 9 September. Two tables: charts and chart_edits. The 37 seeded with real birth details and the timezones the provider resolved, all marked seed and private.

items.title: Chart builds run as a Vercel function
items.note: Done 9 September. POST birth details to /api/chart, get a published link in about 11 seconds. Proven end to end against a production build: place lookup, chart cast, published, served from charts.delphihd.com, synthesis withheld because the tier says free.

items.title: Public birth-details form with account signup
items.note: The form is built at /chart: place chosen from the provider's lookup, birth time asked honestly with a part-of-day fallback, long-form birth certificate guidance and a rectification booking link. An account is created silently from the email they give, with no password and nothing for them to confirm, so their charts are already attached the day there is something to sign into. Mobile: inputs are 16px so Safari does not zoom on focus, and the app declares a viewport.

items.title: Free tier renders the Delphi Basic layer
items.note: Done 10 September. Centres use Delphi Defined/Undefined/Open Basic; channels use Delphi Free Chart; gates now use Delphi Basic, which Kaycee wrote into the gates database on 9 September along with Delphi Bridge Text. All 64 gates carry both. A gate card shows her synthesis when the chart has one and her general words when it does not, the same rule a centre already followed, so a free chart says something real about every gate instead of falling back to a keynote.

items.title: Paid content held back on the free tier
items.note: The synthesis is now withheld by tier, proven on a real chart: free shows 0 of 26 placements and 0 of 9 centres while keeping all 64 gate keynotes. Still to do: the daily transit read becomes subscriber-only.

items.title: Replace the chart tool on the Wix site with an embed
items.note: Done 10 September. Her own form replaced the bodygraph.com widget on the home page hero, desktop and mobile, live at delphihd.com. The old widget collected an email address that went to bodygraph.com; every signup now lands in her own database. The embed only works because /chart carries an exception to the site's no-framing rule, naming her domains AND the Wix sandbox the embed renders inside. Left over: the time of birth field clips slightly on mobile. Kaycee, 2026-09-10: "we can fix that tomorrow."

items.title: Reach the dashboard from anywhere, not just this Mac
items.note: Done 28 September. /portal/admin is the whole dashboard online, behind her sign-in and public.delphi_admins: Everyone, New chart, Status, Transits, Changes, Accounts, Decided and Launch, sortable, with a find box, working on a phone. The 5 AM health check publishes status/health.json so Status is readable away from the Mac. Running a report from here is the piece still to come.

items.title: The chart itself has to work on a phone
items.note: Done 9 September, verified by Kaycee on her own phone. All 37 charts republished with it.

items.title: The chart arrives by email, not just in the tab that made it
items.note: Done 9 September, proven end to end on production: form to chart to inbox, Resend reporting Delivered rather than merely accepted. Sends from chart@send.delphihd.com so the root domain's SPF, which points at Google Workspace, is never touched. Replies go to hello@delphihd.com. Mail can never cost somebody their chart: it is reported, not thrown.

items.title: Sign in and come back to your charts
items.note: Done 5 October. The portal is a sortable, searchable table of every chart on the account with profile, type, authority, definition, personality Sun and birth data, a radio on the row that says which one is you, and Add a chart which does not ask for an email it already has. Charts find their owner: an address on a chart is claimed the first time that person opens the portal, which is how Paul Hollingshead's four and Erlene Goodin's four will arrive whole. Accounts tab on the dashboard shows who has signed up and grants admin or client access, with the last admin protected from removal.

items.title: One gate answer in every view, and the tables follow the chart
items.note: Done 10 September. Each view had grown its own handler, so a gate said something on the bodygraph, less on the mandala and nothing on the astrology ring. One shared function now answers for all four. Hovering a gate or a channel also lights its own placements in the tables, which only the transit column was doing. Mandala channels highlight (their rule was scoped to a canvas the mandala hub is not). Integration channels report a channel the person actually has, and a highlighted one is no longer buried under an overlapping neighbour.

items.title: A transit reads for the date on screen, not the minute the chart was built
items.note: Done 10 September, verified live on 5 June 2027. The two-tone mark was baked at build time, so a gate the chosen date activates could never darken and four gates that only the build minute touched read as transited on every date. Every carried gate now has a sky half and the date decides its colour. All 37 charts republished.

items.title: The free chart cannot be run in a loop
items.note: Done 10 September. The endpoint had no rate limit, no captcha and no origin check, and every call created an account, called the provider, published a file and sent mail. Now limited per email, per caller and site-wide, with a hashed caller rather than a stored address. Accounts are created unconfirmed so none can be squatted, and an address that cannot receive mail is refused before anything is made.

items.title: The astrology section, rebuilt to her list
items.note: Done 5 October and live on all 81 charts. Four angles with rulers, Earth on the wheel from the Human Design data, one set of planet toggles, Placements and Houses split by side, Elements and Modes as split bars, aspects grouped by kind with unaspected bodies, rulerships, dignity, retrograde, Vedic combustion, four house systems, the design chart as a chart in its own right, synastry between the two sides with her orbs, and an aspect grid with hover-only lines.

items.title: The Ascendant at nine o'clock
items.note: Done 3 October, live on all 81 charts since the 5th.

items.title: Transit views in the astrology section
items.note: The engine is built and deployed, 5 October: the renderer can draw a transit outside a chart, and /api/transit-wheel returns a drawn wheel plus transit-to-natal aspects for any date, place and side, cast at Greenwich as UTC by default. NOTHING ON A CHART CALLS IT YET. Still to build: the Transit pill and its three states, the date, time and place picker, the chart picker, and making Bodygraph, Circuits and The Wheel transit views too. Orbs settled: 1 degree, 3 for the Sun, Moon on 3 in its own section.

items.title: Pick a saved chart instead of typing birth details
items.note: The pieces exist as of 5 October: primary_chart_id on the profile, /api/my-charts answering from the session alone, and the chart page proven to share an origin with it so the sign-in reaches it. Still to build: the picker itself, feeding the relationship view and the transit views.

phases.title: Phase 2 — Paid reports
phases.why: The chart they already own fills in with Kaycee's synthesis. Better than a PDF arriving.

items.title: Inngest wired for long jobs
items.note: Reports run seven minutes to two hours, and some fail. Nothing on Vercel or Supabase holds a job that long. Forty attendees with reports included is the case that decides this: forty long jobs, queued with lead time, each retried, each one's failure visible in time to fix it, then the lot released together.

items.title: Stripe checkout in the app
items.note: Account and prices already exist on the Cal.com side. This is wiring, not setup.

items.title: Webhook as the source of truth for what someone owns
items.note: Signature verified before any write. On its own branch, per the git policy.

items.title: Purchase triggers the report, chart republishes with it
items.note: A report becomes visible when it is released, not the moment it is written. A purchase releases it straight away. A batch is held until every report in it is good, because a partial delivery is worse than a late one. So a report needs a state between written and visible, and the chart republishes on release rather than on completion.

phases.title: Phase 3 — Charts for friends and family
phases.why: Highest margin item in the model. No LLM cost at all, just a chart.

items.title: Buy a chart for someone else from inside the portal
Ownership and sharing rules
items.note: Who can see a chart bought for them, and what happens if they make their own account.

items.title: Share a chart with somebody else
items.note: Kaycee, 5 October: "charts always stay with their owners, but I would like them to be able to share them with other people at some point." Nothing ever moves between accounts. The visibility column on charts already carries a shared state, put there in September so these charts would not need a backfill; what is missing is the table of who shared what with whom.

phases.title: Phase 4 — Subscription
phases.why: Unlimited charts plus the daily transit synthesis. Recurring revenue.

items.title: Daily transit run moves to Vercel Cron
items.note: Retires the LaunchAgents on the Mac.

items.title: Transit reads become subscriber-driven, not roster-driven
items.note: Biggest downstream change in the plan. The existing 37 keep working throughout.

items.title: Subscription checkout and lifecycle

phases.title: Phase 5 — Events
phases.why: Kaycee expects to run events regularly. Each one is a different deal, and the machinery should not care which.

items.title: A chart says what its birth time cannot settle
items.note: Done 12 September. A field the scan watches move carries no value: it reads Exact Birth Time Required and opens to what it could be, with the hours each answer covers. The four variables are withheld whenever the time is not exact, whether or not the scan caught them moving. The bodygraph draws solid only what holds at every hour of the window and draws the rest open, so nothing on the picture is ever wrong; a centre says which channels define it, and an unsettled centre no longer wears the label of the hour it was cast at. The astrology wheel draws its angles and house ring open, because the Ascendant crosses the whole zodiac in a day. The dashboard carries a Birth Time column: Exact, Told, Rough, or Rough with the type moving, so a booking arrives with its certainty attached. The scan is stored on the chart row and versioned, so it never re-runs and never serves a stale shape. Measured across 24 birth dates: 42 per cent of six-hour windows move type, profile, authority, definition or the cross.

items.title: An event, with its own terms
items.note: How many people, what they get, when it is live, and what the deal was. Set per event.

items.title: Codes that carry a grant
items.note: Event access, a discount, or a report included. One list, one place to see what has been used.

items.title: Pre-registration, charts built ahead
items.note: The night before rather than thirty at once on venue wifi. Turns the riskiest moment into nothing happening.

items.title: Batch reports, released only when the batch is whole
items.note: Run a day before or the morning of, not on the hour. The batch shows how many are written and how many failed, so failures can be fixed before anybody sees anything. Release is one deliberate act over the whole batch, never per report as each finishes.

items.title: Per-event numbers
items.note: Charts, emails and bookings per event, so she can tell which are worth doing again.

items.title: Tighten the public limit once events are separate
items.note: Forty per connection exists only to survive a room sharing one wifi. Drops to about eight.

decided.what: A chart scans to the LINE and no finer. Colour, tone and base are declared unreliable without an exact birth time rather than searched for, because the Moon crosses a colour every ~17 minutes, a tone every ~3, and a base about every 30 seconds. No scan can bracket that honestly. Kaycee, 2026-09-12: "I like your instinct, let's do that." Consequence: all four variables and both senses are unreliable on any chart without a to-the-minute time, and the chart says so.

How often to sample across a birth-time window is set by the Moon, not a fixed step. Kaycee, 2026-09-12: "Can the scan timing logic be based on the speed of the moon since it's the one that changes most frequently?" The Moon runs between about 11.8 and 15.4 degrees a day depending where it is in its orbit, which is why some days carry far more change than others. Its speed is measured from the two endpoint casts rather than assumed, so it costs nothing extra.

An uncertain chart reports what actually moves on that person's date, not a blanket warning. A blanket warning is noise on a quiet day and nowhere near enough on a busy one. Where nothing moves the chart says so, which is the reassuring and true answer. Fields that move get a mark; clicking it says what it changes to and when. Chart and dashboard stay uncluttered: Kaycee's design.

Everything is compared, not a headline set: the eight properties, all fifteen planets on both sides to gate and line, all nine centres, every channel, all four variables and both senses. A chart is structured data, so comparing two casts is a field-by-field comparison.

Wheel position comes from lib/hd/gate-longitude, the same mapping the mandala is drawn from. Gate numbers are not in wheel order, so subtracting gate numbers says nothing about distance travelled; a second, wrong mapping was written and replaced before it shipped.

Wix wraps every HTML embed in its own sandbox frame served from filesusr.com, so frame-ancestors has to name the sandbox as well as her site. Naming delphihd.com alone leaves the embed blank with no error, which cost an hour. Worth remembering for any future embed.

Owner, Delphi admin and analyst are three separate things in the database now, applied and verified. Kaycee is an admin, so all 37 appear in her portal without an account being created for anybody. No chart was attached to a person: that means creating an account for them, which they should hear about from her rather than discover.

Most people are chart accounts: an account, their charts, no working relationship. Booking a session is what changes it, because that is where it becomes ongoing coaching, and only then is Kaycee their analyst. Her words: "unless they book a session, at that point it really turns into an ongoing coaching kind of situation and changes the relationship, but in general most attendees will just be chart accounts."

An attendee's chart makes Kaycee Delphi admin over it, not their analyst. Running the event is not the same as working with the person; that still takes a booking. So an event fills the funnel without filling her portal with people she has never sat down with.
Events get a code, not their own instance. A second deployment would drift from the real one and split her signups; a code is the same form arriving tagged. Kaycee expects to run events regularly.
An event code RAISES the per-connection limit for its window, never removes it. A leaked code still cannot run away.

Each event carries its own terms, set per event: how many people, what attendees get, when it is live, and a note on the deal. Kaycee, 2026-09-10: "Each one will be slightly different and I want to be flexible."

A free report at an event is not a risk to be capped, it is a cost the event fee already covered. The cap on a code is the number of attendees she was paid for, so the code stops when the deal is fulfilled rather than when a safety number is hit.

Pre-registration publishes the CHART immediately. Reports, when an event includes them, are run with lead time (a day before, or the morning of) and released together only once the whole batch is good. The reason is not theatre, it is that reports fail sometimes: Kaycee, 2026-09-10, "I just don't want to run into a situation where we're running a bunch of reports at the same time and only a handful get theirs because we run into an issue. I would rather resolve the issues and then publish to make it look more seamless." So a report needs a state between written and visible, and a batch needs to be visibly whole before it is released.
Event work is after the 16th. The loose per-connection limit covers her first event on its own; once events carry their own terms the public limit can drop from forty to about eight.

The free chart is protected by a quiet rate limit, not a captcha. Kaycee, 2026-09-10: no visible 'prove you are human' step in front of the hook. Five charts an hour per email address, forty per caller, three hundred site-wide. The caller limit is deliberately loose because a room at an event shares one connection, and a limit tuned to stop a bot would have stopped her whole audience.

No email confirmation step before a chart is sent. You cannot confirm an address without emailing it, so the step would be friction on the hook for no real protection. The account is created UNCONFIRMED instead, so nobody can claim a standing account on somebody else's address, and the rate limit stops volume.
An address that cannot receive mail is refused before anything is created. Every bounce counts against her sending domain.

A chart outlives the account that made it. owner_id was set to cascade, so deleting an account silently deleted its charts; it is now set null. Verified by deleting a throwaway account and watching the chart survive.
charts.delphihd.com added to the Supabase redirect allow list. Magic links could only return to localhost or a Vercel address, so sign-in could never have worked for a real client on her own domain.

The portal lists a person's charts and nothing else, enforced by the database rather than by the query. Proven live: a query asking for all charts with no owner filter returned only that person's two out of thirty-nine.

Chart ownership: most seed clients will own their own account. The Hollingsheads sit under Paul, the Goodins under Erlene. Kaycee sees every chart as Delphi admin, but is only somebody's analyst, with their chart in her own portal, once they book. Schema for this not yet written.
Chart emails send from send.delphihd.com, never the root. One SPF record per domain and hers points at Google Workspace, so a second sender on the apex would have risked hello@delphihd.com.
The free chart never asks anyone to log in. An account is made quietly from their email; login only ever appears at the paid tiers.
The chart email stays plain. Kaycee: "Less to get flagged as spam." A new sending domain has no reputation, and image-heavy first sends are what tip filters.
Inngest for long-running jobs. Kaycee: "I don't want to run anything."
Account required for a free chart, for email capture.
Free basic chart is the hook, not a product. Supersedes the old INTENT line about not being a free chart calculator.
Chart publishes first; the report is added to it on purchase.
Money at the event goes through the existing booking page. No new payment code in launch week.
The dashboard is the one door. Everything else is linked from it, so nothing has to be hunted for.
Signups and emails live in the database, shown on the dashboard. Not Notion: Notion is the source library, not a customer list.

The cloud library was six weeks stale (853 rows, last written 24 July) and four gates had unresolved Quarters. A full sync fixed both: 860 rows, all resolving. Found by comparing a database build against a file build.
The sync runs weekly in GitHub, plus a Sync now button on the dashboard. Kaycee edits the library every few weeks, so nightly was sixty half-hour runs between edits: all risk, no benefit.
The local 3:30am sync LaunchAgent is retired (moved to ~/Library/LaunchAgents/retired, not deleted). One sync, in the cloud.

The birth-time scan casts its sampling grid all at once instead of one after another, and the ceiling went from 14 casts to 48. Kaycee, 2026-09-12: 'Even a stranger on my site deserves good service.' A cast takes about a third of a second, and the grid does not depend on itself, so the old serial version was charging somebody seconds of waiting for nothing. Measured after: a whole-day window is 48 casts in 9.2 seconds, an afternoon 21 casts in 5.5. Charts are unlimited on the Business plan, so the ceiling costs no money, only patience.

The birth-time scan computes planet positions locally (astronomy-engine) to decide which minutes to ask bodygraph.com about, instead of sampling 48 moments across the window. Kaycee, 2026-09-12: 'My vote is for better accuracy.' The split is strict and she asked it be stated plainly: bodygraph.com remains the only authority on what a chart says, including Chiron, Lilith and both nodes; the local maths only decides when to look. Charts are unaffected, byte for byte. Verified against bodygraph.com across three births, both sides, every computable body: worst disagreement 0.64 arcminutes, against a line of 56. The four bodies it cannot compute are the four slowest on the chart, the fastest needing 8.6 days to change a line, so none can move inside a birth window; a bisecting safety net still catches anything the endpoints disagree about that the local maths did not predict.

The scan reports every value a field passes through across the window, not just the first change. Somebody who does not know their birth time cannot use a time, but they can use 'it is one of these three'. This turned up the finding below.

FINDING, needs a product decision: across a six-hour window the four variables are not merely uncertain, they are unknown. Kaycee's own birth date, 12:00 to 18:00: Sense and Design Sense each cycle through all six possible values, Determination through four, Motivation through four. Line-level activations are far steadier over the same window (the Moon moved one gate, everything else a line or none). So an approximate birth time costs the variables entirely while leaving most of the chart intact. The chart should say that specifically rather than warn vaguely about the whole thing.

bodygraph.com's published soft limit is 100K chart pulls a month. Kaycee checked their backend and it recorded 3 pulls for August, so it appears to meter only their own widget and not the API. Treated as uncounted luck, not as budget: everything is planned against the 100K as though it were enforced. At the new ceiling a vague-time chart costs about 35 calls, so 250 of them a month is 12K.

CORRECTION to the finding logged earlier today. That one was drawn from a single birth date and said an approximate time costs the variables while leaving type, profile and authority intact. Kaycee, 2026-09-12: 'can you test against a few more charts so you get a better dataset? The variability day to day fluctuates a lot.' She was right and the single-date reading was wrong. Across 24 birth dates spread over four decades and the lunar year, same six-hour Afternoon window, same place: 42 per cent had type, profile, authority, definition or the cross change inside the window, and 33 per cent had a centre or a channel change. Three changed Type outright (Manifesting Generator to Generator twice, Generator to Projector once), two changed Authority, four changed Profile, four changed Definition. One date, 2 May 2004, changed Type, Strategy, Definition, Signature and Not-self theme together, which is the entire top of the chart. Variables moved on all 24, as before. Moon travel across the window only ranged 2.96 to 3.82 degrees, so how eventful a day is has almost nothing to do with the Moon's speed and everything to do with whether a planet happens to be sitting near a boundary. Kaycee, 2026-09-12: 'it really just depends on what the planets are doing.'

What that means for the product: a general disclaimer is not adequate and a small indicator is not adequate either. For roughly four people in ten with a vague birth time, the thing at the top of their chart is not settled, and a person new to Human Design will read that top line as who they are. The scan runs per person, so nobody needs a generic warning: each chart can say exactly which of its own fields are not settled and what the alternatives are. This is also the honest and non-salesy case for finding a birth certificate or booking a rectification, because for those people it is not a refinement, it is a different chart.

Fields the scan watches move are not given a value. They read 'Exact Birth Time Required' and open, on a click, to what they could be with the hours each answer covers. Kaycee's wording and her instruction. The four variables are withheld whenever the time is not exact, whether or not the scan caught them moving, because they turn over on colour and tone and catching nothing across a sample is luck rather than evidence.

The bodygraph draws solid only what holds across the whole window; anything that comes and goes is drawn open in the colour it would have had. Kaycee, 2026-09-12, choosing between draw-it-anyway, draw-only-what-holds, and withhold-the-picture: '2 seems most inline with our educational purpose.' The effect is that nothing on the drawing is ever wrong, and a beginner can see at a glance which parts of themselves the missing hour is costing them.

An unsettled centre no longer wears the state label of the hour it happened to be cast at, and no longer carries the reading that goes with it. Found by looking at the built chart: a Sacral that is defined for half the window was labelled Undefined and given the whole undefined-Sacral description. Being read the wrong description is worse than being read none.

'I Was Told The Time' runs as exact. Kaycee, 2026-09-12: 'for I was told the time maybe a popup telling them that exact birth time matters, but run the chart as if it were exact.' Only 'I Know Roughly' and 'I Don't Know It' are scanned, so a told or documented time costs no extra calls at all.

Every possible answer a withheld field could take carries Kaycee's own short text on hover, so the difference between Generator and Projector can be seen rather than just named. Kaycee, 2026-09-12: 'it would help people see the difference and why it matters... I know I still need to add Delphi Basic columns to some of the databases, it's a top priority of mine, but I'd like the function to be there.' Built to read whatever exists: Gates (all 64) and Profiles (all 12) work today; Type, Authority, Definition, Channels and the variables are wired and start working on the first sync after she writes those columns. Nothing needs changing in the code when she does.

A remembered time says its piece in a note under the birth time pills rather than in a popup, matching the existing note for a rough time. Kaycee, 2026-09-12: 'maybe not a popup, but the added text underneath the birth time pills like the unknown time.'

The note under a rough birth time no longer says Type and Authority are usually reliable. The 24-date measurement had Type changing on three of them, and somebody in that three would have read the reassurance on the form and then met 'Exact Birth Time Required' on their own Type a minute later. New wording: the variables are out of reach, Profile, Ascendant and sometimes Type can change, and the chart says which of their own details are settled.
The badge on a withheld field reads '2 Possible' rather than 'could be 2'. Kaycee, 2026-09-12.

20260912_birth_time_scan.sql is APPLIED. Run through the SQL editor in Kaycee's own browser rather than handed to her as instructions. Verified after: a rough-time chart scans in 3.8 seconds and 43 calls the first time, returns instantly and identically the second, and rescans correctly when the birth time is edited (Afternoon window became the Morning window, cast for 9:00 AM).

MEASURED, needs a decision before the event. The whole chart is built inside the web request, which has a 120 second ceiling. Six people with no birth time submitting at the same moment: every chart succeeded, and every one took 29 seconds. The scan is about 42 of the calls in each. Extrapolating the same shape, roughly 25 people at the same instant is where the ceiling is. Caching does not help this, because it only saves the rebuild and every one of these is a first build. BFKI is pre-registration spread over days rather than a room submitting at once, which is the main thing making this survivable, but a group hitting signal together after a day with none is exactly Kaycee's stated situation.

Two open questions closed by the day's work. The local ephemeris was added and is now the source for the birth time scan and all four cycle dates, with bodygraph.com still the only authority on Human Design itself. And the pacing and retry for bodygraph.com's rate limit went into the shared layer, so every caller is protected and not just the scan.

The cycle pills are off the transit tab. They jumped the view to a cycle's date and kept whatever time of day the picker was on, so the chart drawn was that date at an arbitrary hour rather than the moment of the return. Kaycee compared her Uranus Opposition against Maia Mechanics: Maia has it at 20:48 UTC, this drew 7:07 PM local. The dates themselves are sound and stay on the Dates tab.

Return charts: the hard part is done and proved. A cycle chart is the connection endpoint called with the person's birth and the return moment, so bodygraph.com computes the four connection types itself, and those are exactly the classification the method uses: Dominance is Educational, Electromagnetic and Compromise are Personal, a bare gate activation is Environmental. It also returns the return's own design side, which landed within a minute of both Maia Mechanics and our own calculation. Kaycee's Uranus Opposition came back with 5 dominances, 5 electromagnetics, 3 compromises and a 4/6 cycle profile. What is left is plumbing a Cycle mode that reuses the relationship drawing, which is deliberately left until after the 14-18 September event: every builder change today needed all 46 charts republished and several surfaced edge cases, and that risk should not land on the week the charts need to be stable.

The Incarnation Cross text is found by angle, Personality Sun and the four gates, never gates alone. Fifty quads in her Crosses database are two crosses (a Juxtaposition and an angled one) so the old key let one overwrite the other: twenty live charts read another cross's words from 09-13 until now. Publishing refuses a chart whose cross text names a different cross. Fifteen Cross fields in Notion were corrected with her; five with a wrong gate (JC of Possession, JC of Empowering, JC of Oppression, JC of Bargains, LAC of Endeavor) are still open and need her eye. A daily check over all 194 pages runs in the 5 AM health report.

Variations is live on every chart, between Individual and Transit: one card per stretch of the birth day where the reading changes, cast on first open (about ten seconds) and kept in storage. Opening a card shows the cross, the centres and both placement tables, with a purple pill for a gate that moved and a gold underline for a line that moved. Her words approved 09-17 and 09-20.

The event stats page carries Incarnation Cross (split by version, grouped by cross) and Variables (PXX DXX, with Unknown for times that are not exact), each with her Delphi Basic on hover. Someone who signs up more than once counts once, by their newest sign-up.

On a chart whose time is not exact, only what actually changes across the day is drawn unfinished. A line move is not a gate move; a gate a steady planet holds all day is hers; each leg is judged on its own side; a centre defined at every hour is defined even when the wiring changes; a channel with one certain end keeps that end. Found on Sabrina Carpenter's 25, 4 and Ajna.

The daily transit report runs on GitHub Actions at 6 AM Mountain year round, not on her Mac. It publishes to storage, /t/<date> serves it behind a key, and a LaunchAgent collects it into HD Reports → Transits so Evening Echoes and the health check are unaffected. The report retries any synthesis that comes back empty (on 09-28 the model returned 17 of 25 and three gate popups shipped blank). The dashboard has a Transits page listing each day's link.

The workshop deck, the Stage, the Living Mandala tables, the worksheet, the light QR card and the chart builder's local-only Stage switches are committed. They had lived only on her Mac since the BFKI workshop, which is why the nightly repo pull had refused to run since 09-17. docs/WORKSHOP_STAGE.md now records how to rebuild the tool for the next event.

A chart that is missing a section is not published at all. The builder refuses a page short a bodygraph, mandala, astrology wheel, placement tables or panel, and a failed astrology cast throws instead of logging and finishing the page. Jim Jones' chart was wanted for its astrology and shipped without it, because the provider does not know a place called Lynn, Indiana.

Every astrology wheel is anchored on the Ascendant, at nine o'clock: the chart page, the saved image and both sides of the relationship wheel. The fixed-zodiac anchor was chosen for overlays, but reading houses is what the wheel is for. Charts published before today keep the old orientation until they are rebuilt, which is Kaycee's call.

Charts are made from the dashboard. New chart posts to /api/admin/chart, gated on public.delphi_admins, with the four funnel columns as selectors: how they got here, birth time accuracy, tier, and who can see it. It retires the terminal for add-public-figure and make-sandbox-charts and uses the same runBuilder every other chart goes through. It does not replace add-client.ts, which takes a real client all the way through reports, folder and Notion row. Not /api/chart either, which is the public form and carries rate limits, account creation and an email.

Astro-cartography is a planned module, not scheduled. Kaycee's requirements, recorded so they are not re-derived: it exists to compare the personality and design maps, each viewable on its own and both together, and it is offered only for known birth times. Groundwork already in place: birth coordinates are geocoded and cached for every chart, and astronomy-engine is already a dependency (lib/hd/ephemeris.ts), so the right ascension and declination the lines need are computable in house. The provider cannot supply them; its astrology endpoint returns ecliptic longitude only. An angular line moves about 15 degrees of longitude per hour of birth time, which is why rough and unknown times are excluded rather than drawn open.

Where to see what is built: the dashboard's Launch tab is the single answer, and it is kept current rather than written once. A chart-facing change is only on a chart after a republish, so the dashboard now shows when charts were last rebuilt beside when the site last deployed. Kaycee, 5 October: "I need to be able to see all of this somewhere to fully understand what you are talking about."

Whether the test chart made on 9 September to prove the email path (a second copy of Kaycee's own) is deleted or kept as a sample to show people.

Planetary returns may want to be drawn like a relationship chart rather than a date on the transit view: the return overlaid on the natal chart, two states at once. Kaycee, 2026-09-10: the cross of the Uranus Opposition factors into a reading, so how the returns are displayed needs reconsidering. Parked by her the same day, not dropped.

Captcha on the auth endpoints is off. Supabase's per-IP limits are the only guard on sign-in, and per-IP limits do not stop anything distributed. Worth turning on if abuse ever appears; it needs a Turnstile or hCaptcha key.

The site refuses to be embedded in a frame by anyone (frame-ancestors none, X-Frame-Options DENY). Correct as a default, but the Wix embed will be blocked by it until an exception is carved out for the chart form alone.

Ownership schema: owner, Delphi admin, and analyst-of are three different things and today owner_id is being asked to mean all three, which is why no chart is attached to anyone. Needs a migration and policies before real people are invited.
http://localhost:3000/** is on the production redirect allow list. Dev convenience left in production; low risk, worth removing before launch.

The dashboard birth time reliability indicator is not built yet. Everything it needs now exists on the chart row once the migration is applied: time_accuracy, and time_scan carrying whether the identity fields are among the casualties.

Whether to deliver the chart first and scan after, rebuilding in the background, so nobody waits on the scan. It would take each person's wait back to roughly what an exact time costs and remove the event ceiling risk entirely. It changes how a chart is made, so it is Kaycee's decision, not a side effect.

Left on unknown birth times: the astrology view still draws its angles and house ring as though the hour were known. Kaycee approved the treatment on 2026-09-12 ('1- yes, 2-let's handle it the same') and the groundwork is in and dormant: the wheel knows its angles are never settled without an exact time, and the Moon's signs across the window are read locally. Nothing draws them yet.

Return charts, properly. Kaycee, 2026-09-12: 'we need to remove the return chart pills from the transit page, they still aren't entirely accurate and it will be important that they are for this part.' Three things a real return chart needs that a transit view cannot give it. The exact moment, not the date: 'The line on the sun/earth placements is incredibly important as it's a profile that sets the tone for the cycle', and a line is about a hundred minutes of solar travel. Its own design side, about 88 solar degrees before the return, exactly as a birth chart has. And probably its own drawing, closer to a relationship chart than a transit: the return laid over the natal, two states at once, which she first raised on 2026-09-10 about the Uranus Opposition cross. The moments are already computed to the second and verified against Swiss Ephemeris, so the arithmetic is done; the chart is not.
